criteria.note: bash test_cli_runner.sh: pass.cases.json exits 0 (6/6 cases across echo/printf/false/cat/sh/true incl nonzero-exit and stdin); fail.cases.json exits 1, naming both broken expectations (stdout_contains and exit_code). check_result genuinely asserts exit_code, stdout_equals, stdout_contains (list-aware), stderr_contains; max_seconds enforced via subprocess.run(timeout=) with TimeoutExpired returning a failure early - a live sleep 5 vs max_seconds 1 test failed with exit 1, so a timeout is never a pass. not_found also returns a failure. Commands run as a real subprocess with no shell (no shell=True; argv list passed to execve), so sh -c in a fixture is the author's explicit choice, not injection.
Tamper: copied pass.cases.json, changed case0 exit_code to 42, ran the runner -> FAIL 'exit_code: expected 42, got 0', overall exit 1. The runner does not pass a false assertion.

Assertions reflect real observed behavior: subprocess.run captures actual returncode/stdout/stderr and measures wall-clock elapsed; timeout is a genuine subprocess kill verified live. Nothing stubbed.

python3 scripts/selftest.py: 161 passed / 0 failed. cli-runner block drives the fixture pair (pass -> passed True, fail -> passed False, names the broken expectation) and exercises check_result directly (clean on match; loud on wrong exit code, missing substring, and timeout) using hand-built dicts and trivial POSIX commands - no external dependency. capabilities.yaml marks cli_process_runner status: reference and is byte-identical across both copies (.warp/ and plugin/templates/.warp/). Runner + fixtures + selftest block are generic (grep for bcengi/travelpass/workpass/dejitech/dmitry/coreconnect/daybook found nothing).

findings.text: By design ('a case asserts only what it declares'), a case with an empty expect {} passes as long as the command runs, and a degenerate stdout_contains/stderr_contains of "" is vacuously satisfied since every string contains the empty substring. This is documented behavior and cannot rubber-stamp any real (non-empty) assertion - every genuine declared expectation, plus timeout and command-not-found, is properly asserted (proven by the tamper and live-timeout tests). Note only, not blocking.
